pages.title: Deskbot – ESP32 AI Desktop Assistant | IOTA JU
pages.text: Deskbot – ESP32 AI Desktop Assistant | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS Project Deskbot An ESP32-powered, voice-controlled AI desktop study assistant streaming audio to Gemini AI for hands-free, screen-free learning and accessibility. Project Summary Deskbot is an ESP32-powered, voice-controlled AI desktop study assistant designed to answer academic questions hands-free. It captures spoken questions, streams audio to a Python backend powered by Gemini AI, and speaks back the answers in real time. Alongside an integrated focus timer and clock to minimize phone distractions, it provides an accessible, screen-free learning device particularly helpful for visually impaired users and individuals with limited mobility. Project Overview System Architecture & Workflow The end-to-end communication pipeline links micro-hardware to cloud AI: 1 Audio Input: The onboard microphone on the ESP32 captures the user's speech and streams 16-bit PCM audio packets over Wi-Fi using the UDP protocol. 2 Backend Processing: A dedicated Python application receives the UDP stream, converts speech to text (STT), and forwards the prompt to the Gemini API. 3 Synthesis & Output: Gemini’s generated answer is converted back into speech (TTS) and streamed over UDP to the ESP32, which plays it out via an amplifier and speaker. Engineering Challenges & FreeRTOS Implementation 1 Audio Bottleneck: Handling continuous audio streaming without packet loss or blocking network traffic was a primary technical hurdle. 2 Multi-Task Architecture: The team utilized FreeRTOS to implement distinct parallel tasks for microphone recording, Wi-Fi packet reception, and speaker playback. 3 Buffer Management: Incoming audio packets are temporarily queued in a memory buffer to absorb network jitter and packet arrival variations, ensuring glitch-free playback. Implementation Result 1 Hands-Free Academic Q&A: Successfully processed spoken questions and delivered accurate, spoken answers in clear natural language without requiring a display screen, keyboard, or mouse. 2 Real-Time Voice Pipeline: Achieved end-to-end processing—capturing spoken audio on the ESP32, streaming it via UDP over local Wi-Fi, transcribing via STT, generating an answer via Gemini API, synthesizing the speech, and playing it back through the desktop speaker. 3 Tabletop Productivity Tools: Ran an integrated tabletop digital clock alongside a dedicated study/focus timer, keeping time visible to prevent study distractions and eliminate phone pickups. 4 Accessibility Interface: Provided a viable assistive device for visually impaired users and people with limited motor skills by replacing complex website navigation and typing with direct voice interaction. pages.title: Gamepad – 8-Bit Handheld Retro Console | IOTA JU
pages.text: Gamepad – 8-Bit Handheld Retro Console | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS Project Gamepad A custom-engineered, standalone 8-bit handheld console running an extensible object-oriented C++ game engine with 7 playable titles including 3D raycasted DOOM. Project Summary A custom-engineered, standalone 8-bit handheld console powered by an ATmega328P microcontroller running on a custom 2-layer PCB designed in KiCad. The system utilizes an extensible object-oriented C++ game engine to execute seven classic titles, including a raycasted 3D DOOM demake on a 128 x 64 monochrome OLED screen. By leveraging non-volatile flash memory (PROGMEM) and fixed-point arithmetic, the console achieves real-time physics and rendering under strict 2 KB SRAM limitations within an ergonomic 3D-printed enclosure. Project Overview The project transitions classic breadboard retro-gaming concepts into a robust, integrated consumer-grade embedded system. The hardware core features an ATmega328P MCU driving a high-contrast I2C OLED display alongside a tactile pushbutton control interface routed onto a custom, compact PCB. On the software layer, rather than hardcoding static game loops, a polymorphic engine structure was built around a Finite State Machine (FSM). This modular architecture decouples display drivers, input debouncing, and game state loops, allowing scalable expansion across 7 titles: Space Trash, Breakout, T-Rex Run, DOOM, Snake, Space Wars, and Tetris. The firmware is optimized for extreme memory constraints through bitwise operations, custom collision algorithms, and static memory allocation to avoid heap fragmentation. 3D DOOM Demake Space Trash Breakout T-Rex Run Snake Space Wars Tetris Hardware Stack Processor: ATmega328P (16 MHz, 5V logic) Display: 0.96-inch monochrome SSD1306 OLED (128 x 64, I2C interface) PCB Design: Custom 2-layer PCB routed in KiCad (optimized trace routing, active pull-ups, power decoupling) Inputs: Tactile digital momentary pushbuttons Software & Toolchain Stack Language/Environment: C++, Arduino IDE Core Architecture: Object-Oriented Polymorphic Engine, Finite State Machine (FSM) Memory Optimization: Flash asset allocation via PROGMEM, Fixed-Point Math, Bit-masking CAD / EDA Tools: KiCad (Schematic capture & PCB layout) Back to Projects © 2026 IoT Applications Club, Jadavpur University. pages.text: MediGuard – AI & IoT Based Smart Medicine Verification System | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS 2026 Project MediGuard – AI & IoT Based Smart Medicine Verification System Reducing medication errors by verifying both the patient and the medicine before consumption using biometric and deep vision edge intelligence. Project Summary MediGuard is an intelligent healthcare system designed to reduce medication errors by verifying both the patient and the medicine before consumption. It combines fingerprint authentication with AI-based medicine image verification using an ESP32-S3 camera system. A dedicated Android application manages patient details, medicine enrollment, and medication schedules, while Firebase and a Flask backend provide cloud connectivity and data processing. Project Overview MediGuard consists of an ESP32-S3 based embedded device integrated with an OV3660 camera, AS608 fingerprint sensor, OLED display, and speaker. Patients are authenticated using their fingerprint, after which the system retrieves their scheduled medication. The medicine is captured through the device camera and compared with previously enrolled reference images using a computer-vision pipeline based on image preprocessing, MobileNetV2 embeddings, and cosine similarity. The verification result is then communicated through the OLED and audio feedback. The Android application provides a centralized interface for patient registration, fingerprint enrollment, medicine enrollment, and schedule management. Hardware Stack ESP32-S3 N16R8 (Dual-Core AIoT SoC) OV3660 Camera Module AS608 Optical Fingerprint Sensor 1.3-inch OLED Display Speaker / Audio Module Power Bank / Portable Power Supply Software Stack Arduino C++ / ESP32 Firmware Android Application (Java) Flask / Python Backend Firebase Firestore EasyOCR MobileNetV2 Cosine Similarity REST APIs Wi-Fi Communication Implementation Result A functional working prototype of MediGuard has been developed. The system successfully integrates fingerprint-based patient authentication, medicine reference-image enrollment, camera-based medicine verification, Firebase data management, and Android-based patient and schedule management. The ESP32-S3 communicates with the Flask backend over Wi-Fi, while verification results are displayed on the OLED and provided through audio feedback. The complete workflow—from patient authentication and medicine identification to verification and result generation—has been implemented and demonstrated. Optimized for Raspberry Pi hardware, it serves as a robust tool for automated infrastructure auditing and vehicle safety. pages.text: SMART AI Powered Study Guide and Ebook Reader | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us Arduino SSCS Challenge 2026 SMART AI Powered Study Guide and Ebook Reader An ESP32-based multi-capability study companion combining offline eBook reading, FTP server, Bluetooth A2DP audio streaming, macro remote keypad, and Android AI assistant. Your browser does not support the video tag. Summary An ESP32-based EBook reader engineered to provide a distraction-free, screen-efficient learning experience with comprehensive peripheral and cloud connectivity: eBook Reading & Storage: Read and store extensive eBook collections with up to 32GB SD card storage support. FTP File Server: Functions as an active FTP server on the home network for wireless file management. Bluetooth Audio Streaming: Store and stream ambient background study audio directly to external Bluetooth speakers. Bluetooth Macro Keypad: Operates as a remote Bluetooth keypad to control smartphones or laptops. AI Companion App: Dedicated Android companion app that parses study notes, generates AI flashcards, and syncs them automatically to the device. SSCS Standards: Designed following the official Arduino SSCS Challenge 2026 guidelines. Overview & Firmware Architecture Core Firmware Libraries Adafruit_SSD1306 & Adafruit_GFX (or U8g2): Drives the OLED display, performing low-level pixel manipulation, font rendering, line wrapping, and dynamic reader UI management. SD.h / FS.h: Manages the FAT file system on the SD module to traverse directories, stream large .txt files into memory buffers, and store incoming notes. ESP32-A2DP: Implements the Advanced Audio Distribution Profile (A2DP) source mode to stream I2S audio wirelessly to paired speakers. BluetoothSerial.h: Manages Classic Bluetooth Serial Port Profile (SPP) connections for receiving raw note payloads over the air. Keypad.h: Handles button matrix polling, hardware debouncing, and translation into navigational and media macro triggers. Dual Data Pipeline Management The ESP32 acts as a central hub managing concurrent display and wireless communication pipelines: Display Pipeline: When reading, text chunks are fetched from the SD card into RAM, formatted by the graphics engine, and pushed to the SSD1306 OLED over I2C/SPI. Button polling triggers instantaneous text buffer paging. Wireless Transfer & Audio: Audio macros invoke ESP32-A2DP audio encoding, while the BluetoothSerial SPP stream receives mobile text pushes and directly writes them to the SD card via the FS library—acting as a wireless flash drive. Companion Android Application Built completely in Android Studio with Kotlin and native toolchains, the mobile companion application inputs notes and documents in PDF format. pages.text: SpinSafe: Predictive Maintenance | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us SpinSafe: Edge-Native Predictive Maintenance Transforming legacy industrial machinery into self-diagnosing smart hardware through high-speed, closed-loop ML architecture. Industrial Revolution at the Edge SpinSafe is an autonomous predictive maintenance system designed to modernize legacy industrial motors. By shifting intelligence from the cloud to the hardware itself, it enables sub-second reaction times to mechanical anomalies. The system utilizes a retrofittable hardware node that captures multi-axis vibration, temperature, and electrical load data, processing it through a local AI gateway that retrains its models every 10 seconds to adapt to each specific motor's "healthy" baseline. Core Innovations Dynamic Baseline Learning: Retrains a Decision Tree classifier every 10 seconds to detect unique precursors to failure. Hardware-Level Interrupts: Bypasses network latency to cut power in milliseconds during critical failures. Multi-Sensor Fusion: Integrates MPU6050 vibration analysis with thermal and current telemetry. Zero-Cloud Dependency: Operates fully at the edge, ensuring security and maximum uptime for industrial networks. Legacy Integration: Designed as a retrofittable node for rapid deployment across existing motor fleets. textBlocks.text: Deskbot – ESP32 AI Desktop Assistant | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS Project Deskbot An ESP32-powered, voice-controlled AI desktop study assistant streaming audio to Gemini AI for hands-free, screen-free learning and accessibility. Project Summary Deskbot is an ESP32-powered, voice-controlled AI desktop study assistant designed to answer academic questions hands-free. It captures spoken questions, streams audio to a Python backend powered by Gemini AI, and speaks back the answers in real time. Alongside an integrated focus timer and clock to minimize phone distractions, it provides an accessible, screen-free learning device particularly helpful for visually impaired users and individuals with limited mobility. Project Overview System Architecture & Workflow The end-to-end communication pipeline links micro-hardware to cloud AI: 1 Audio Input: The onboard microphone on the ESP32 captures the user's speech and streams 16-bit PCM audio packets over Wi-Fi using the UDP protocol. 2 Backend Processing: A dedicated Python application receives the UDP stream, converts speech to text (STT), and forwards the prompt to the Gemini API. 3 Synthesis & Output: Gemini’s generated answer is converted back into speech (TTS) and streamed over UDP to the ESP32, which plays it out via an amplifier and speaker. Engineering Challenges & FreeRTOS Implementation 1 Audio Bottleneck: Handling continuous audio streaming without packet loss or blocking network traffic was a primary technical hurdle. 2 Multi-Task Architecture: The team utilized FreeRTOS to implement distinct parallel tasks for microphone recording, Wi-Fi packet reception, and speaker playback. 3 Buffer Management: Incoming audio packets are temporarily queued in a memory buffer to absorb network jitter and packet arrival variations, ensuring glitch-free playback. Implementation Result 1 Hands-Free Academic Q&A: Successfully processed spoken questions and delivered accurate, spoken answers in clear natural language without requiring a display screen, keyboard, or mouse. 2 Real-Time Voice Pipeline: Achieved end-to-end processing—capturing spoken audio on the ESP32, streaming it via UDP over local Wi-Fi, transcribing via STT, generating an answer via Gemini API, synthesizing the speech, and playing it back through the desktop speaker. 3 Tabletop Productivity Tools: Ran an integrated tabletop digital clock alongside a dedicated study/focus timer, keeping time visible to prevent study distractions and eliminate phone pickups. 4 Accessibility Interface: Provided a viable assistive device for visually impaired users and people with limited motor skills by replacing complex website navigation and typing with direct voice interaction. textBlocks.text: Gamepad – 8-Bit Handheld Retro Console | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS Project Gamepad A custom-engineered, standalone 8-bit handheld console running an extensible object-oriented C++ game engine with 7 playable titles including 3D raycasted DOOM. Project Summary A custom-engineered, standalone 8-bit handheld console powered by an ATmega328P microcontroller running on a custom 2-layer PCB designed in KiCad. The system utilizes an extensible object-oriented C++ game engine to execute seven classic titles, including a raycasted 3D DOOM demake on a 128 x 64 monochrome OLED screen. By leveraging non-volatile flash memory (PROGMEM) and fixed-point arithmetic, the console achieves real-time physics and rendering under strict 2 KB SRAM limitations within an ergonomic 3D-printed enclosure. Project Overview The project transitions classic breadboard retro-gaming concepts into a robust, integrated consumer-grade embedded system. The hardware core features an ATmega328P MCU driving a high-contrast I2C OLED display alongside a tactile pushbutton control interface routed onto a custom, compact PCB. On the software layer, rather than hardcoding static game loops, a polymorphic engine structure was built around a Finite State Machine (FSM). This modular architecture decouples display drivers, input debouncing, and game state loops, allowing scalable expansion across 7 titles: Space Trash, Breakout, T-Rex Run, DOOM, Snake, Space Wars, and Tetris. The firmware is optimized for extreme memory constraints through bitwise operations, custom collision algorithms, and static memory allocation to avoid heap fragmentation. 3D DOOM Demake Space Trash Breakout T-Rex Run Snake Space Wars Tetris Hardware Stack Processor: ATmega328P (16 MHz, 5V logic) Display: 0.96-inch monochrome SSD1306 OLED (128 x 64, I2C interface) PCB Design: Custom 2-layer PCB routed in KiCad (optimized trace routing, active pull-ups, power decoupling) Inputs: Tactile digital momentary pushbuttons Software & Toolchain Stack Language/Environment: C++, Arduino IDE Core Architecture: Object-Oriented Polymorphic Engine, Finite State Machine (FSM) Memory Optimization: Flash asset allocation via PROGMEM, Fixed-Point Math, Bit-masking CAD / EDA Tools: KiCad (Schematic capture & PCB layout) Back to Projects © 2026 IoT Applications Club, Jadavpur University. textBlocks.text: MediGuard – AI & IoT Based Smart Medicine Verification System | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us IEEE SSCS 2026 Project MediGuard – AI & IoT Based Smart Medicine Verification System Reducing medication errors by verifying both the patient and the medicine before consumption using biometric and deep vision edge intelligence. Project Summary MediGuard is an intelligent healthcare system designed to reduce medication errors by verifying both the patient and the medicine before consumption. It combines fingerprint authentication with AI-based medicine image verification using an ESP32-S3 camera system. A dedicated Android application manages patient details, medicine enrollment, and medication schedules, while Firebase and a Flask backend provide cloud connectivity and data processing. Project Overview MediGuard consists of an ESP32-S3 based embedded device integrated with an OV3660 camera, AS608 fingerprint sensor, OLED display, and speaker. Patients are authenticated using their fingerprint, after which the system retrieves their scheduled medication. The medicine is captured through the device camera and compared with previously enrolled reference images using a computer-vision pipeline based on image preprocessing, MobileNetV2 embeddings, and cosine similarity. The verification result is then communicated through the OLED and audio feedback. The Android application provides a centralized interface for patient registration, fingerprint enrollment, medicine enrollment, and schedule management. Hardware Stack ESP32-S3 N16R8 (Dual-Core AIoT SoC) OV3660 Camera Module AS608 Optical Fingerprint Sensor 1.3-inch OLED Display Speaker / Audio Module Power Bank / Portable Power Supply Software Stack Arduino C++ / ESP32 Firmware Android Application (Java) Flask / Python Backend Firebase Firestore EasyOCR MobileNetV2 Cosine Similarity REST APIs Wi-Fi Communication Implementation Result A functional working prototype of MediGuard has been developed. The system successfully integrates fingerprint-based patient authentication, medicine reference-image enrollment, camera-based medicine verification, Firebase data management, and Android-based patient and schedule management. The ESP32-S3 communicates with the Flask backend over Wi-Fi, while verification results are displayed on the OLED and provided through audio feedback. The complete workflow—from patient authentication and medicine identification to verification and result generation—has been implemented and demonstrated. textBlocks.text: SMART AI Powered Study Guide and Ebook Reader | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us Arduino SSCS Challenge 2026 SMART AI Powered Study Guide and Ebook Reader An ESP32-based multi-capability study companion combining offline eBook reading, FTP server, Bluetooth A2DP audio streaming, macro remote keypad, and Android AI assistant. Your browser does not support the video tag. Summary An ESP32-based EBook reader engineered to provide a distraction-free, screen-efficient learning experience with comprehensive peripheral and cloud connectivity: eBook Reading & Storage: Read and store extensive eBook collections with up to 32GB SD card storage support. FTP File Server: Functions as an active FTP server on the home network for wireless file management. Bluetooth Audio Streaming: Store and stream ambient background study audio directly to external Bluetooth speakers. Bluetooth Macro Keypad: Operates as a remote Bluetooth keypad to control smartphones or laptops. AI Companion App: Dedicated Android companion app that parses study notes, generates AI flashcards, and syncs them automatically to the device. SSCS Standards: Designed following the official Arduino SSCS Challenge 2026 guidelines. Overview & Firmware Architecture Core Firmware Libraries Adafruit_SSD1306 & Adafruit_GFX (or U8g2): Drives the OLED display, performing low-level pixel manipulation, font rendering, line wrapping, and dynamic reader UI management. SD.h / FS.h: Manages the FAT file system on the SD module to traverse directories, stream large .txt files into memory buffers, and store incoming notes. ESP32-A2DP: Implements the Advanced Audio Distribution Profile (A2DP) source mode to stream I2S audio wirelessly to paired speakers. BluetoothSerial.h: Manages Classic Bluetooth Serial Port Profile (SPP) connections for receiving raw note payloads over the air. Keypad.h: Handles button matrix polling, hardware debouncing, and translation into navigational and media macro triggers. Dual Data Pipeline Management The ESP32 acts as a central hub managing concurrent display and wireless communication pipelines: Display Pipeline: When reading, text chunks are fetched from the SD card into RAM, formatted by the graphics engine, and pushed to the SSD1306 OLED over I2C/SPI. Button polling triggers instantaneous text buffer paging. Wireless Transfer & Audio: Audio macros invoke ESP32-A2DP audio encoding, while the BluetoothSerial SPP stream receives mobile text pushes and directly writes them to the SD card via the FS library—acting as a wireless flash drive. Companion Android Application Built completely in Android Studio with Kotlin and native toolchains, the mobile companion application inputs notes and documents in PDF format. It can either direct-port them to the IoT device over Bluetooth or leverage AI models to generate interactive study flashcards. The app also supports music file transmission and local summary archiving. textBlocks.text: SpinSafe: Predictive Maintenance | IOTA JU Home Events Projects Team Timeline Alumni About Us SpinSafe: Edge-Native Predictive Maintenance Transforming legacy industrial machinery into self-diagnosing smart hardware through high-speed, closed-loop ML architecture. Industrial Revolution at the Edge SpinSafe is an autonomous predictive maintenance system designed to modernize legacy industrial motors. By shifting intelligence from the cloud to the hardware itself, it enables sub-second reaction times to mechanical anomalies. The system utilizes a retrofittable hardware node that captures multi-axis vibration, temperature, and electrical load data, processing it through a local AI gateway that retrains its models every 10 seconds to adapt to each specific motor's "healthy" baseline. Core Innovations Dynamic Baseline Learning: Retrains a Decision Tree classifier every 10 seconds to detect unique precursors to failure. Hardware-Level Interrupts: Bypasses network latency to cut power in milliseconds during critical failures. Multi-Sensor Fusion: Integrates MPU6050 vibration analysis with thermal and current telemetry. Zero-Cloud Dependency: Operates fully at the edge, ensuring security and maximum uptime for industrial networks. Legacy Integration: Designed as a retrofittable node for rapid deployment across existing motor fleets.
